target_customer: Fundamental equity funds with $1B to $10B in assets (Kimpton OS) and AI labs that need finance training and evaluation environments (Koliseum, EvalRouter)
problem: Active managers trail benchmarks and funds stitch together point tools or babysit general agents; AI labs lack evaluation that cannot be rehearsed or backdated.
business_model: B2B software for funds plus data and evaluation environments sold to AI labs (pricing not public)
product_category: Financial AI research OS and live evaluation benchmarks

founders.name: Jack Zumwalt
previous_startups: Level III Capital (co-founded quantitative systematic trading fund; outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: co-founded Level III Capital and managed its daily operations; previously a detection engineer at Goldman Sachs. Education not listed.

founders.name: Mauricio Ortiz
founders.background_notes: YC page: oversaw technical implementation of the investment process at Level III and was on Goldman's critical infrastructure team (consumer bank and Apple Card systems). His bio also labels him CEO, which conflicts with the CTO title.

founders.name: Adrian Del Bosque
founders.background_notes: YC page: founding engineer at Level III who built trading infrastructure; before that senior cloud and platform engineer at Vistra; began at SpaceX on Automation and Controls.

competitors.name: Hebbia
competitors.what: AI platform for document heavy financial research and diligence
competitors.traction_then: Vendor page claims over 40 percent of the largest asset managers by AUM use it (self reported)

competitors.name: AlphaSense
competitors.what: Market intelligence and AI search for finance

competitors.name: Rogo
competitors.what: AI for investment banking and finance professionals
competitors.traction_then: Directory listing says 35,000 professionals across 250+ firms (unverified)
competitors.funding_then: Series D of $160M in April 2026 per one directory

technical_complexity.rationale: Producing structured trade proposals and building point in time financial environments that avoid leakage requires institutional data integration and careful evaluation design.

defensibility.rationale: A live track record and a public benchmark can build credibility, but funded platforms like Hebbia, Rogo and AlphaSense already serve institutions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known; well funded finance AI platforms existed at founding.

market_need_then: The company points to active managers trailing benchmarks and capital moving to passive funds, and to labs needing non leaking evaluations; its founders report a live first client managing $3.3B.

branding.domain_note: Uses kimpton.ai; kimpton.com belongs to the hotel brand.

identity.visual_style: Minimal layout with short direct copy
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and concise, with lines such as 'AI should answer to reality'

branding.brand_signature: Public EarningsBench benchmark and the line 'We build what AI learns from'

brand_strength.rationale: Name collides with the Kimpton hotel brand in search results, and no press on the brand was found; the benchmark could build attention later.

outcome_analysis: Kimpton is a Spring 2026 company built by three engineers who ran a quantitative fund and productized its stack. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. Its early signals are a live institutional client reported by the company and a public benchmark, while risks are heavily funded finance AI incumbents and a name that collides with a hotel brand.
notes: Funding: Neuronfeed lists $500K seed in January 2026 without investors, single aggregator, unverified and not recorded as a round. The $10M raised from a family office at age 21 and 22 and scaled to $35M belongs to the founders' earlier fund (Level III Capital), not to Kimpton, so it is not a round; the ages come from the company's own text and are not recorded per founder. The Kimpton OS $3.3B client is company reported. Competitor entries lack exact source dates.
